title.narrative: Women economic resilience in times of climate crisis

description.narrative: Kenya’s floriculture sector is a major contributor to the national economy, driving the gross domestic product (GDP) growth, exports, and employment. Women make up about 80% of its workforce, yet they remain highly vulnerable—facing low wages, insecure contracts, gender-based violence, and limited decision-making power. Climate-related crises such as floods and droughts compound these risks, disrupting food security and increasing living costs. The floods of March 2024 in Kenya highlighted critical gaps in gender-sensitive climate adaptation, crisis preparedness, and social safety nets. Despite ongoing sustainability efforts, the absence of living wages and inclusive response systems continues to leave women disproportionately exposed to economic and social shocks.The “Women’s Economic Resilience in Times of Climate Crisis” project, funded by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) under the SPVO/SSF programme (SPVO25S001), aims to address these challenges. In Phase A (June–December 2025), Women Win, Bloomon, Sian Flowers, and CIFCAD will carry out an in-depth local impact assessment and due diligence analysis. Using surveys, interviews, and participatory tools such as Drawing the Line, the project will examine how climate crises affect women workers’ working conditions, wages, health, and safety, and identify adaptive strategies to strengthen their long-term resilience.The project will directly benefit more than 1,200 women employed across Sian Flowers’ farms in Kenya. Additional beneficiaries include Sian male workers as allies, Sian Flowers, Bloomon, and sector stakeholders such as the Kenya Flower Council, who will gain from improved due diligence practices and shared learnings.By December 2025, the project will deliver a stakeholder-validated action plan with concrete measures to reduce identified social risks. Ultimately, this project aims to enhance women’s economic resilience, advance gender-responsive policies such as fair wages and safer working conditions, and embed social sustainability into climate resilience strategies, creating a more resilient floriculture value chain.
